Checklist.heading: Settlement Checklist
Checklist.descriptionAuth: Check off procedures as you complete them.
Checklist.descriptionGuest: Sign in to track your progress.
Checklist.congratsMessage: You have completed all settlement procedures. Welcome to Norway!

1.title: Receive job offer from Norwegian employer
1.guidance: Your employer handles this step. The contract must meet UDI requirements for skilled worker permits.

2.title: Apply for skilled worker residence permit via UDI
2.guidance: Apply online at udi.no — search for 'skilled worker residence permit'. Your employer may also need to submit documentation.

3.title: Book biometrics appointment at Norwegian embassy/consulate
3.guidance: Contact your nearest Norwegian embassy or consulate to book a biometrics appointment. Find locations at norway.no.

4.title: Apply for D-number from Skatteetaten
4.guidance: Visit your local tax office (skattekontor) in person. Find your nearest office at skatteetaten.no — search for 'skattekontor'.

5.title: Open Norwegian bank account
5.guidance: Contact a Norwegian bank (e.g. DNB, SpareBank 1, Nordea) with your D-number and valid passport. Most banks allow starting the process online.

6.title: Obtain tax card (skattekort) from Skatteetaten
6.guidance: Apply online at skatteetaten.no — search for 'skattekort'. Your employer needs this before your first payslip.

7.title: Register with NAV
7.guidance: Register as a jobseeker at nav.no or visit your local NAV office. This gives you access to Norwegian welfare services.

8.title: Register with a GP (fastlege)
8.guidance: Register for a GP at helsenorge.no — search for 'bytte fastlege'. You need a D-number or personnummer first.

9.title: Register with the National Population Register (Folkeregisteret)
9.guidance: Register in person at your local tax office (skattekontor). Find your nearest office at skatteetaten.no — search for 'folkeregisteret'.

10.title: Obtain national ID number (personnummer)
10.guidance: Issued automatically by Skatteetaten after you have lived in Norway for at least 6 months and registered in the Folkeregisteret.

11.title: Apply for Norwegian national ID card
11.guidance: Apply at your local police station (politistasjon). Book an appointment at politiet.no — search for 'nasjonalt ID-kort'.

12.title: Prepare documentation of family relationship
12.guidance: Gather marriage certificates, birth certificates, and passport copies. Documents may need to be translated and apostilled.

13.title: Apply for family reunification residence permit
13.guidance: Apply online at udi.no — search for 'family immigration'. The reference person in Norway must also submit documentation.

14.title: Attend interview at Norwegian embassy/consulate
14.guidance: The embassy will contact you to schedule an interview after your application is submitted. Bring all original documents.

15.title: Receive admission letter from Norwegian educational institution
15.guidance: Apply to Norwegian institutions through their own admission portals, or through samordnaopptak.no for public universities.

16.title: Show proof of financial support
16.guidance: You must demonstrate sufficient funds for one academic year. Check current amounts at udi.no — search for 'financial support student'.

17.title: Apply for student residence permit
17.guidance: Apply online at udi.no — search for 'student residence permit'. Apply early, as processing times can be several weeks.
